I need to find the characteristic polynomial of the given matrix, which is given by $\det(A - \lambda I)$.

First, I'll set up the matrix $A - \lambda I$:

$$A - \lambda I = \begin{pmatrix}
-4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14-\lambda
\end{pmatrix}$$

Now I'll compute the determinant using cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)\begin{vmatrix}
10-\lambda & 4 \\
-5 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} - (-13)\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 4 \\
12 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} + 10\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 10-\lambda \\
12 & -5
\end{vmatrix}$$

Let me calculate each 2×2 determinant:

First determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
10-\lambda & 4 \\
-5 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} = (10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(-5)$$
$$= -140 - 10\lambda + 14\lambda + \lambda^2 + 20$$
$$= \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$$

Second determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 4 \\
12 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} = (-9)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(12)$$
$$= 126 + 9\lambda - 48$$
$$= 9\lambda + 78$$

Third determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 10-\lambda \\
12 & -5
\end{vmatrix} = (-9)(-5) - (10-\lambda)(12)$$
$$= 45 - 120 + 12\lambda$$
$$= 12\lambda - 75$$

Now substituting back:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(9\lambda + 78) + 10(12\lambda - 75)$$

Expanding the first term:
$$(-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) = -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480$$

Expanding the other terms:
$$13(9\lambda + 78) = 117\lambda + 1014$$
$$10(12\lambda - 75) = 120\lambda - 750$$

Adding all terms together:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480 + 117\lambda + 1014 + 120\lambda - 750$$

Combining like terms:
- $\lambda^3$ term: $-\lambda^3$
- $\lambda^2$ term: $-8\lambda^2$
- $\lambda$ term: $104\lambda + 117\lambda + 120\lambda = 341\lambda$
- Constant term: $480 + 1014 - 750 = 744$

Therefore, the characteristic polynomial is:

$$\boxed{-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744}$$
